en.title: Ways to Split an Array into Non-Decreasing and Non-Increasing Arrays
en.description:
Given a positive integer array arr, count the pairs of non-negative integer arrays b and c, both of length n, such that b is non-decreasing, c is non-increasing, and b[i]+c[i]=arr[i] for every i. Output the answer modulo 1000000007.

The standard input/output, the ranges added by this site, and the examples follow this problem's description; wherever the source's ranges are missing, they are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n (1≤n≤3000); the second line contains n integers (1≤arr[i]≤3000). The ranges and the modulus are taken from the original problem's constraints.
en.output: Output the number of ordered array pairs (b,c) that satisfy the conditions, modulo 1000000007.
en.explanation: Given the previous term b[i−1], the next term x=b[i] must be at least b[i−1]+max(0,arr[i]−arr[i−1]) and must also satisfy x≤arr[i]. Maintaining the number of ways for each ending value together with its prefix sums gives an O(n·max(arr)) transition.
hints: Given the previous term b[i−1], the next term x=b[i] must be at least b[i−1]+max(0,arr[i]−arr[i−1]) and must also satisfy x≤arr[i]. Maintaining the number of ways for each ending value together with its prefix sums gives an O(n·max(arr)) transition.
